question.text: Which of the following makes an issuer INELIGIBLE for an IPO under Regulation 5 of SEBI ICDR?

answer.text: The issuer has outstanding ESOPs that are fully paid up
The issuer has net tangible assets below Rs. 3 crore
A promoter of the issuer is a wilful defaulter
The issuer has changed its name in the preceding year

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 5 of SEBI ICDR makes an issuer ineligible for an IPO if the issuer or any of its promoters or directors is a wilful defaulter or a fraudulent borrower. Qualifying ESOPs are specifically exempted from the convertible-securities bar. The Trap: Net tangible assets of at least Rs. 3 crore is an eligibility condition under Regulation 6, not an ineligibility condition under Regulation 5; an issuer that does not meet Regulation 6 may still use the alternative QIB route. Note: Regulation 5 lists the ineligibility grounds (wilful defaulter, fraudulent borrower, etc.), while Regulation 6 sets out the affirmative eligibility conditions such as net tangible assets and the QIB route.
